title: Use a substitution like u = 1 + sqrt(x) to clear a square root from the denominator before integrating
content: When an integrand has a square root sitting inside a denominator, e.g. x/(1+sqrt(x)), a substitution of the form u = 1 + sqrt(x) turns the whole denominator into the single variable u, since sqrt(x) = u - 1 means x = (u-1)^2 and dx = 2(u-1) du. Substituting throughout converts the integral into a polynomial-over-u integral in u only (here, 2(u-1)^3/u), which you can then expand the numerator, divide term-by-term by u (the 1/u term integrates to ln u), and integrate as normal. Don't forget to convert the limits of integration from x-values to u-values using the same substitution before evaluating.
